targetWords.definition: An alliance is a group of people who work together.
targetWords.example: The junior executives formed an alliance with each other.

targetWords.definition: Applause is the noise made when people clap hands to show approval.
targetWords.example: At the end of his speech, everyone gave applause.

targetWords.definition: If you are armed, you are carrying a weapon.
targetWords.example: The robber was armed with a gun.

targetWords.definition: If something is authoritative, it uses the best information available.
targetWords.example: This book is an authoritative source on Ancient Egypt's Queen Nefertiti. ce re m o n y [seramouni] n.

targetWords.definition: -» Tom and Amy's marriage ceremony is in June.
targetWords.example: Tom and Amy's marriage ceremony is in June.

targetWords.definition: Culture is the music, art, and writings of a certain place or group of people.
targetWords.example: Ancient Mexican culture is renowned for its architecture. d e fe n s e [difens] n.

targetWords.definition: -» The airforce works in defense of its country.
targetWords.example: The airforce works in defense of its country. d e ta il [dliteil] n.

targetWords.definition: -»Jane told Ben all the details of her trip to China.
targetWords.example: Jane told Ben all the details of her trip to China.

targetWords.definition: When a group of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things. Big cities have diverse populations with people of different races and ages.
The beautiful woman enchanted everybody in the room.
To equip someone is to give them the things needed to do something.
targetWords.example: Steve was equipped with the tools needed to do the job.

targetWords.definition: An exception is someone or something not conforming to a rule.
targetWords.example: Most students thought the test was hard, but Tim was the exception. genre [3d:nr0] n.

targetWords.definition: -* She is considered a master in the comedy genre.
targetWords.example: She is considered a master in the comedy genre.

targetWords.definition: — My grandmother had a great impact on my life.
To lure someone is to convince them to do something, by using a trick.
targetWords.example: The store lures people in with big signs that say "Sale!"

targetWords.definition: An obstacle is an object or a problem that stops you from doing something.
targetWords.example: Climbing over the giant rock was the biggest obstacle for the hikers. shelter [feitar] n.

targetWords.definition: -» The frog took shelter from the storm in a nearby cave.
targetWords.example: The frog took shelter from the storm in a nearby cave.

targetWords.definition: To sort means to separate things into different groups or classes.
targetWords.example: He sorted his clothes by colors and sizes.

targetWords.definition: To supply something means to give people what they need or want.
targetWords.example: The water heater supplied the house with warm water.

targetWords.definition: If people are vain, they are only concerned with how they look.
targetWords.example: Rebecca is so vain that she looks at herself in every mirror.

story.passage:
Sometimes famous people are vain. They only care about themselves. But Josephine

Baker was an exception. In the 1930s and 1940s, Baker was one of the most famous

women in France. She was a big part of the new jazz genre and culture and had a diverse

group of fans. The French people especially loved her. And she loved France. So when

World War II started, she wanted to help the nation that had given her so much.

In 1940, armed German troops entered Paris. When this happened, some French

people formed a secret alliance. It was called the French Resistance. The group worked

for the defense of France. It helped the European and American armies fight the

Germans.

Baker was an important member of the Resistance. She had three

jobs. The first was to carry messages to and from other members.

The messages were written in code on her sheets

of music. The second was to provide shelter and

supply goods to Resistance members. It would have

been dangerous if the Germans found them.

Baker's third job was the most important. Baker held

concerts for European politicians and army members.

She lured them in, promising an entertaining show.

She enchanted them with her singing and dancing

and got lots of applause.

But Baker was

L

always equipped

A

with a small

notebook at these

concerts. She listened

for details about the war and wrote

them down. Baker sorted the details and gave

authoritative reports to the Resistance.

Some thought Baker's fame would be an obstacle. The

Germans knew who she was, but they didn't think she was smart

enough to work for the Resistance. So she could get information

from the Germans easily. This helped the Resistance and the

French army save lives and win the war.

Baker had a big impact on the Resistance's work. She got

many awards for her help. When she died, the army had a special

ceremony to thank her again for her bravery.
